extracted.intended_audience: companies, sustainability professionals, policymakers, and the general public interested in corporate climate targets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for companies to set, validate, and govern science-based greenhouse gas emission reduction and net-zero targets aligned with climate science and the Paris Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with climate science and Paris Agreement goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Help companies to set emission reduction targets in line with climate sciences and Paris Agreement goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SBTi was established to help companies set emission reduction targets that are consistent with the best available climate science and the objectives of the Paris Agreement. The initiative's frameworks and standards aim to ensure corporate targets collectively support limiting warming (see net-zero standard and 1.5 °C limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-practice transition planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice as identified by SBTi is for companies to adopt transition plans covering scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, set out short-term milestones, ensure effective board-level governance and link executive compensation to the company's adopted milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBTi recommends comprehensive transition plans that address direct (scope 1), indirect energy-related (scope 2), and value-chain (scope 3) emissions; include short-term milestones to track progress; establish board-level oversight; and align executive incentives with milestone achievement. Use of these elements is presented as SBTi best practice for credible target setting and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net-zero corporate standard (limit warming to 1.5 °C)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi developed and launched the world's first net zero standard, providing the framework and tools for companies to set science-based net zero targets and limit global temperature rise above pre-industrial levels to 1.5 °C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The net-zero standard (launched October 2021) is the formal framework companies can use to define and validate net-zero commitments; targets should be consistent with limiting warming to 1.5 °C. Companies seeking SBTi validation are expected to follow the standard's requirements and use the provided tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific methodologies and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi developed separate sector-specific methodologies, frameworks and requirements for different industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBTi issues tailored guidance per sector to reflect differing emissions profiles and decarbonization pathways. As of September 2024, sector guidance exists (with statuses) for aluminium (scoping), apparel and footwear (finalized), aviation (in development), buildings (finalized), chemicals (in development), cement (finalized), financial institutions (finalized), Forest, Land and Agriculture (finalized), ICT (finalized), land transport (in development), maritime (finalized), oil and gas (paused), power (finalized), and steel (finalized). Companies should consult the applicable sector methodology for specific requirements and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position and rules on carbon offsets / environmental attribute certificates (EACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: In April 2024 the SBTi Board of Trustees released a statement setting out an intention to permit the use of environmental attribute certificates (EACs) for abatement purposes against Scope 3 emissions reduction targets; SBTi did not previously permit the use of EACs due to difficulties in tracing, measuring and validating their impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents a material policy change with significant debate: the page records controversy (including staff protest and media attention) and notes arguments that carbon offsets/EACs are incompatible with the Paris Agreement. Companies and validators must follow the Board's formal policy language and be aware of ongoing scrutiny and sector reactions when using EACs for Scope 3 claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLAG guidance allowing insetting for target claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Launched in September 2022, the SBTi's Forestry, Land and Agriculture (FLAG) guidance allows companies to claim the achievement of their emission reduction targets through 'insetting', breaking from the long-held SBTi position that emission reduction targets should only be achieved through emission reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FLAG guidance permits 'insetting' approaches in certain circumstances, but the page notes that insetting is a business-driven concept not defined in international standards or guidelines (e.g., ISO 14050, IWA 42), which has contributed to debate about its appropriateness and integrity. Companies using FLAG guidance should understand the definitions, limits, and scrutiny around insetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of targets by SBTi Services (commercial validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi Services, a commercial subsidiary, offers to validate climate targets set by companies as science-based targets for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation is a formal process provided by the initiative's commercial arm. Companies seeking the SBTi 'science-based' validation must submit targets for assessment against SBTi criteria and may pay fees for services. The existence of a paid validation pathway and the organization's governance are relevant to questions of independence, capacity, and procedural expectations.
